simple.meaning: מְצוּרָה (mᵉtsûwrâh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a hemming in, i.e. (objectively) a mound (of siege), or (subjectively) a rampart (of protection), (abstractly) fortification.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at 2 Chronicles 11:10. The surrounding context includes birth, family, family line, firstborn, kingship, city.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מְצוּרָה (H4694) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

timeline.evidenceText: Zorah, Aijalon, and Hebron, which are fortified cities in Judah and in Benjamin.
He fortified the strongholds, and put captains in them, and stores of food, oil and wine.
He dealt wisely, and dispersed of all his sons throughout all the lands of Judah and Benjamin, to every fortified city. He gave them food in abundance and he sought many wives for them.
He took the fortified cities which belonged to Judah, and came to Jerusalem.
Also he took away out of all the cities of Judah the high places and the sun images; and the kingdom was quiet before him.
Their father gave them great gifts of silver, of gold, and of precious things, with fortified cities in Judah; but he gave the kingdom to Jehoram, because he was the firstborn.
I will encamp against you all around you, and will lay siege against you with posted troops. I will raise siege works against you.
For Yahweh restores the excellency of Jacob, as the excellency of Israel; for the destroyers have destroyed them, and ruined their vine branches.
